rules.description: Framework surfaces exist at the repository root
rules.what: A required harness surface is missing from the repository root.
rules.why: The framework only works as a reusable bootstrap when its root instructions, state files, scripts, and docs are discoverable in consistent locations.
rules.fix: Restore the missing root file or directory, or update the documented framework contract before changing the repository layout.

rules.description: Feature tracker preserves WIP=1, dependency order, and lane ownership
rules.what: feature_list.json allows multiple active features, an active feature with unmet dependencies, or (on a lane/<feature-id> branch) an active feature that does not match the lane's declared feature.
rules.why: The harness depends on a single active feature and explicit dependency ordering to keep sessions scoped, resumable, and verifiable. Worktree lanes (feat-010, D-017) extend this per-branch: a lane branch may only activate the feature it is named for, so concurrent lanes stay independently auditable.
rules.fix: Set at most one feature to active and ensure its dependencies are already passing before resuming implementation. On a lane/<feature-id> branch, the active feature must be <feature-id> — activate that feature or switch lanes.

rules.description: Framework docs are project-specific, not template placeholders
rules.what: Core framework docs still contain placeholder template text.
rules.why: Reusable harness instructions must describe the actual framework contract; placeholder docs create false confidence and mislead downstream adopters.
rules.fix: Replace template copy in README, docs/PRODUCT.md, and docs/quality-document.md with framework-specific guidance and current state.

rules.description: Harness manifest accurately declares reusable and instance surfaces
rules.what: The manifest is missing, malformed, or declares surfaces that do not exist in the repository.
rules.why: The reusability contract depends on a machine-readable classification of CORE, INSTANCE, and optional components; a manifest that drifts from the repo makes upgrades and adoption unpredictable.
rules.fix: Repair .harness/manifest.json so every declared surface exists and matches the repository layout.

rules.description: Every tracked file is classified by the seam manifest (or exempted as product-owned)
rules.what: A tracked file is not declared as CORE, INSTANCE, TEMPLATE, or product-owned (productRoots or the docs/ default) in the manifest, or is declared twice.
rules.why: Reusability requires that distribution can answer, for every file, whether it ships as-is, ships as a skeleton, never ships, or belongs to the adopting project. Unclassified files get silently dropped or silently leaked — both break the seam contract.
rules.fix: Classify the file in .harness/manifest.json (core / instance / templates), or add its parent directory to productRoots if it is product-owned outside docs/.

rules.description: Feature declarations carry no inline mutable state; sharded state stays consistent
rules.what: A feature_list.json entry still declares state/status/evidence inline, or a file under .harness/state/ is invalid JSON, has an invalid state, or does not correspond to any declared feature.
rules.why: Sharded feature state (feat-011, D-017) only delivers conflict-free lane landings if feature_list.json truly stays declaration-only and every shard is a real, valid record of one feature's current state — drift here silently reintroduces the whole-file race the sharding exists to remove.
rules.fix: Run `node scripts/framework-check.mjs migrate-feature-state` to move inline state/evidence into .harness/state/<id>.json, or fix/remove the invalid or stray shard file.
